/itineraryStops/5/whyOnRoute.source_en: After the Joseon-and-Silla heritage block of Gyochon and Woljeonggyo, this is **the one stop of the day in the present tense**. Daereungwon has no stairs and no climb — flat grass paths make it the easiest walking of the day — and one wall further on there is coffee and red-bean bread on Hwangnidan-gil. The fact that **a royal tomb and a cafe are a one-minute walk apart** is itself the character of this city. Late afternoon is when Hwangnidan-gil is at its liveliest, and it lets guests handle **restrooms, coffee and souvenirs in one place** before the final stop (the museum, or Donggung & Wolji). The **actual** gold crown is at ⟦G0⟧, the next stop — so seeing the excavation site at Cheonmachong and then the artifact at the museum makes **the order itself the story**.

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/parking.source_en: Paid car park at the Daereungwon main gate

/itineraryStops/5/convenience/restroom.source_en: Public restrooms at the Daereungwon main gate and near Cheonmachong · in-store restrooms when you use a Hwangnidan-gil cafe

/itineraryStops/5/description.source_en:
**Daereungwon** is a tomb park of **126,500 m²** of gentle grass mounds holding **23 tombs of Silla kings, queens and nobles**, most of them raised in the **4th–6th centuries**. The most famous is **Cheonmachong (Tomb 155)** — **excavated on April 16, 1973**, 12.7 m high and about 47 m across, and **the only tomb in Daereungwon whose interior is open to visitors**. The dig produced **11,526 artifacts**, among them the **Cheonmachong Gold Crown (National Treasure No. 188)** and the **Cheonmado — the only Silla-era painting that survives**, drawn on a birch-bark saddle flap (the crown itself is on display later in the day, at ⟦G0⟧). Neighbouring **Hwangnamdaechong** is the largest tomb in the complex: its twin north and south mounds hold **an unidentified Silla king and queen buried together**, and the queen's gold crown carries **3 pairs** of pendants where a king's normally carries one — a hint at how high Silla's early royal women stood. **Park admission is free** (Cheonmachong's interior costs adult ₩3,000 / youth ₩2,000 / child ₩1,000). Climbing the mounds is prohibited. 

**Directly across Daereungwon's west wall** is **Hwangnidan-gil**. The name fuses **Hwangnam-dong with Gyeongnidan-gil** (Seoul's Itaewon street) — it literally means **'Hwangnam-dong's Gyeongnidan-gil'**. Running **from Naenam Intersection to the Hwangnam Elementary School intersection**, both sides are lined with **cafes, restaurants, studios and gift shops converted out of hanok houses**, and **since around 2017** it has been the youngest street in Gyeongju. This neighbourhood is also the home of **Hwangnam bread** — the thin wheat pastry filled with red-bean paste **first made in 1939 in Hwangnam-dong by Choi Yeong-hwa**, and the souvenir travellers carry out of Gyeongju more than any other. 

Because tombs and cafe street are separated by **a single wall**, this tour walks **1,500 years and the 2020s side by side on one drop-off**.

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Daereungwon 09:00–22:00 (to 21:00 in winter) · Hwangnidan-gil shops generally 10:00–21:00 (varies by shop)

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Easy — flat grass paths between the mounds (126,500 m²), comfortable for strollers and older guests. Hwangnidan-gil is a flat pavement

/itineraryStops/5/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Daereungwon park free · Cheonmachong interior adult ₩3,000 / youth ₩2,000 / child ₩1,000 · Hwangnidan-gil itself free

/itineraryStops/6/category.source_en: National museum of Silla artifacts — replaced Nov–Feb by the Donggung & Wolji night view

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/1.source_en: Silla History Hall + Silla Art Hall (≈20 min) / winter: one loop of the pond (≈25 min)

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/2.source_en: Wolji Hall + the outdoor Emille Bell (≈20 min) / winter: night-view photography (≈20 min)

/itineraryStops/6/timeUsed/3.source_en: Cheonmachong Gold Crown room (≈10 min) / winter: waiting for the lights to come on (≈10 min)

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/0.source_en: **Mar–Oct = ⟦G0⟧** / **Nov–Feb = Donggung & Wolji by night** — a last stop the season decides

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/1.source_en: **Cheonmachong Gold Crown (National Treasure No. 188)** — the actual crown from the tomb you saw at the previous stop

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/2.source_en: **Emille Bell / Sacred Bell of King Seongdeok (National Treasure No. 29)** — cast 771 CE, ~19 tons, among the largest bronze bells extant

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/3.source_en: **Wolji Hall = 33,000+ artifacts from the 1975–1976 dredging of Wolji** — the twin of Donggung & Wolji

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/5.source_en: **Open as normal on Mondays** — regular closures are Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok only

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/6.source_en: **Donggung & Wolji = Historic Site No. 18**, the Silla detached palace and pond created in 674 by King Munmu (formerly Anapji)

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/7.source_en: Donggung & Wolji **09:00–22:00 (ticketing closes 21:30) · open year-round · adult ₩3,000**

/itineraryStops/6/highlights/8.source_en: Winter sunset **17:15–17:30** — arriving about 17:00 means you watch it from dusk to illumination

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/tip.source_en: No flash photography; some special exhibitions prohibit all photography (check signage); allow ~10 minutes for the bell pavilion alone — it is the single most important Silla artifact

/itineraryStops/6/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Museum shop with replica gold-crown jewelry; café in the main building; cloakroom available
